title: A finite union of sets D(f) ∩ V(g_1,…,g_n) in an affine spectrum is a finite disjoint union of such sets
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $\operatorname{Spec}A$ its spectrum [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Call a subset of $\operatorname{Spec}A$ *basic* if it is of the form $D(f)\cap V(g_1,\dots,g_n)$ with $f,g_1,\dots,g_n\in A$, $n\ge0$, where $D(f)=\{\mathfrak p:f\notin\mathfrak p\}$ and $V(g_1,\dots,g_n)=\{\mathfrak p:g_1,\dots,g_n\in\mathfrak p\}$. If $B_1,\dots,B_m\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$ ($m\ge0$) are basic, then there are finitely many basic subsets $C_1,\dots,C_p\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$ ($p\ge0$), pairwise disjoint, with $B_1\cup\dots\cup B_m=C_1\cup\dots\cup C_p$.

source.place: no single place: the refinement step 'After refining the partition further' of Etale Cohomology, Lemma Tag 03S0 (etale-cohomology.tex line 12049), for the basic sets of Algebra, Lemma Tag 0G1P (algebra.tex line 5434); compare Topology, Lemma Tag 09Y4 (topology.tex line 5607), which refines a finite family of constructible sets into a disjoint stratification by constructible sets but does not keep the pieces basic

proof.text: (The inductive construction.) We construct by induction on $t=0,\dots,m$ a finite pairwise-disjoint family $\mathcal C_t$ of basic subsets with $\bigcup\mathcal C_t=B_1\cup\dots\cup B_t$. Put $\mathcal C_0=\emptyset$ (empty union). Given $\mathcal C_t=\{C_1,\dots,C_q\}$, define $\mathcal R$ as follows: start with the one-element family $\mathcal R_0=\{B_{t+1}\}$; for $l=1,\dots,q$ let $\mathcal R_l$ be obtained from $\mathcal R_{l-1}$ by replacing every member $P$ by the finite pairwise-disjoint family of basic sets with union $P\setminus C_l$ given by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-basic-set-difference]; put $\mathcal R=\mathcal R_q$. By induction on $l$, $\mathcal R_l$ is a finite family of basic sets, pairwise disjoint (pieces coming from the same $P$ are disjoint by that node, pieces coming from distinct members $P\ne P'$ of $\mathcal R_{l-1}$ are disjoint because $P\cap P'=\emptyset$), with $\bigcup\mathcal R_l=B_{t+1}\setminus(C_1\cup\dots\cup C_l)$. So $\mathcal R$ is a finite pairwise-disjoint family of basic sets with $\bigcup\mathcal R=B_{t+1}\setminus\bigcup\mathcal C_t$.

(The new family.) Put $\mathcal C_{t+1}=\mathcal C_t\cup\mathcal R$. It is finite, and pairwise disjoint: members of $\mathcal C_t$ are pairwise disjoint by the inductive hypothesis, members of $\mathcal R$ are pairwise disjoint by Step 1, and a member of $\mathcal R$ is contained in $B_{t+1}\setminus\bigcup\mathcal C_t$, hence disjoint from every member of $\mathcal C_t$. Its union is $\bigcup\mathcal C_t\cup(B_{t+1}\setminus\bigcup\mathcal C_t)=\bigcup\mathcal C_t\cup B_{t+1}=B_1\cup\dots\cup B_{t+1}$. After $m$ steps, $\mathcal C_m$ is the required family (for $m=0$ it is empty). (The delivered proof formed the family from the pieces of $C\setminus B_{t+1}$ for $C\in\mathcal C_t$ together with $\mathcal R$, whose union is the symmetric difference and omits $\bigcup\mathcal C_t\cap B_{t+1}$; corrected by L, found by the worker of the difference node.)
